summary: Montgomery Peak lookout west of Red Bluff: a telephone was added c.1930 and a county station completed in 1932; FFLA lists it gone. Site today not described.

facts.design: Enclosed tower; a 20-foot lookout station with an observation floor above living quarters (1932 report)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the FFLA California list. No source gives the date or cause.

staffing.status: a 1932 newspaper item said Elmer Peasley would go on duty June 1; no later report found

events.note: A lookout at the Montgomery ranch was already in use; a telephone was being installed to speed reports
A May 1932 report says a county lookout on Montgomery Peak was completed that week. It may or may not be the same station as the 1930 ranch lookout.

evidence.supports: 1930 telephone being installed to speed reports from the Montgomery ranch lookout
evidence.quote: are today installing a telephone on Montgomery Peak to speed up reports from the Montgomery ranch lookout.

evidence.supports: dated July 8, 1930: two rural fire department members installing the telephone
evidence.quote: Merrill Swain and Roy Wright, members of the rural fire department, are today installing a telephone on Montgomery Peak

evidence.supports: before the telephone, the lookout walked several hundred yards to report a fire
evidence.quote: Formerly it was necessary for the lookout to travel several hundred yards to the ranch headquarters to report a fire.

evidence.supports: county lookout on Montgomery Peak completed in May 1932
evidence.quote: Construction of a county lookout on Montgomery Peak west of Red Bluff has been completed this week

evidence.supports: Elmer Peasley due on duty June 1 in the new 20-foot station
evidence.quote: Elmer Peasley will go on duty June 1 in the new 20 foot lookout station.
The upper floor is for observation and below is the living quarters.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the type as an enclosed tower
FFLA lists the lookout as gone

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two sources, both used. Newspaper items are quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the FFLA list gives the type and status. A search for Montgomery Peak lookout history found nothing further. The 1930 item calls it the Montgomery ranch lookout; the 1932 item reports a new county lookout on Montgomery Peak; the sources do not say whether they are one station. Record kind enclosed_tower matches FFLA; no correction proposed. No photo found. Site today not described by any source.
